articles.title: Why Tiny JPEGs Look Different in Chrome
articles.summary: A clever JPEG decoding optimization in Chrome has been causing tiny images to look different on various computers, with some appearing thicker and more faithful to the original image than others. This issue is due to how JPEG compression works, specifically a technique called Discrete Cosine Transform that converts images into frequency domain data. The optimization involves scaling down images at small scales before decompressing them in memory, which can be wasteful and lead to information loss, especially in high-frequency detail areas.
